kitPage.title: Seiðr-kit — showcase
kitPage.lead: Every shared LORE v2 element on one page, as it looks in the dark amber Seiðr theme, on colour tokens and the --fs-2xs…--fs-2xl scale.
kitPage.pal.lead: Ctrl+K — records and commands, “/” — search records; with no query — recent items. Keys work in any keyboard layout.
kitPage.el.fresh: Freshness cell — column fresh:<field>, thresholds come from the app
kitPage.sh.sheetBody: Side panel: focus is trapped inside, Esc closes it.
kitPage.sh.nested: List inside a record — a passport's children and links: search, filter, grouping and order are the same as in sections; a reference outside the export stays a row with a note.
kitPage.sh.ctlbar: The control bar on its own — for tables that draw their own rows (tree, task table): search, facets, grouping and order are the same parts and the same model as in a list.
kitPage.merge.title: Disputed blocks (concurrent edit)
kitPage.merge.lead: The record was changed during the edit: non-overlapping blocks merge by themselves, a line diff only for the block both sides edited.

admin.title: Admin
admin.agents.title: Agents
admin.agents.lead: Which harness each agent runs in, on which machine and whose it is. “Not set” and “not linked” mean no data, not “as intended”.
admin.agents.truncated: Not all agents shown: the server truncated the result.
admin.rules.title: CLAUDE rules
admin.rules.lead: CLAUDE rules docs (kind claude-rules): body and versions. The comparison view depends on what the server returns.
admin.rules.fileNote: The rules file lives on the machine — neither the browser nor the server can see it. The doc-vs-file diff is computed by MCP claude_rules_diff; sync is claude_rules_push and claude_rules_pull.
admin.rules.pickHint: Pick a rules doc to see its body and versions.
admin.rules.unknownDoc: Doc {id} is not among CLAUDE rules.
admin.rules.htmlOnly: The doc has only an HTML body — MD bodies are shown here.
admin.rules.outsideScope: Versions exist but are outside your projects — this is not "no history".
admin.rules.noVersions: The doc has no SCD2 versions: writing a doc does not create versions — nothing to compare.
admin.rules.oneVersion: The doc has one version — nothing to compare with.
admin.rules.pickVersion: Which version to compare with the previous one
admin.rules.coarse: The texts are long — the diff is coarse: everything removed and everything added as a whole.
admin.rules.noBodies: The server does not return version bodies — no line diff; body changes are visible by hash.
admin.col.author: Author
admin.flags.title: Flags and version
admin.flags.lead: Which build LORE runs and which lore.* flags differ from their defaults.
admin.flags.releaseNone: the deploy did not pass a release tag
admin.flags.noneChanged: All flags are at their defaults.
admin.harness.dictEmpty: The harness dictionary is empty — the migration has not run yet. Editing is unavailable, shown as is.
admin.harness.dictError: Could not read the harness dictionary ({reason}) — editing is unavailable, shown as is.
admin.who.title: People and their projects
admin.who.lead: How many projects each person is in, their role in each and their agents. An agent sees all of its owner’s projects, so a project runs the agents of all its members.
admin.who.agentsError: Agents could not be read ({reason}) — people and roles shown, agents not.
admin.who.orphans: Agents without an owner among people ({n}):
admin.log.title: Action journal
admin.log.lead: Who changed what in LORE: when, in which family, over which record, human or agent, and how it ended. Refusals are as visible as successes.
admin.log.emptyHint: No mutating calls in admin families yet: a verified zero, not a failed read.
admin.log.emptyFilterHint: The journal is not empty — no record just fits these conditions. Clear the filter to see the whole journal.
admin.log.forbiddenHint: Only an administrator sees the action journal. This is not an empty journal — it was not given to you.
admin.log.badParamsAllowed: The server listed the allowed values:
admin.log.totalExact: Showing {shown} of {total} records under the filter.
admin.log.totalUnknown: Records shown: {shown}. How many there are in total under the filter is unknown: the server could not count. That is neither zero nor «all of them».
admin.log.truncated: Output cut by the limit of {limit}: there are more records than shown. Raise the limit or narrow the period.
admin.log.truncatedNoLimit: Output was cut: there are more records than shown, and the server did not name the limit. Narrow the period.
admin.log.f.timeHint: Period: a date (2026-11-10), an ISO instant (2026-11-10T12:00:00Z) or epoch millis. A date in «To» takes the whole day.
admin.log.batch.nothing: There is nothing to expand: no role events carry this batch id. This is not «the batch was empty» — that is how batches applied before this rollout, dry runs and no-op batches look.
admin.log.batch.error: The batch did not expand ({reason}) — a failed read, not «no such batch». You can retry.
admin.log.batch.undoOpen: The undo window is still open — until {until}.
admin.log.batch.undoClosed: The undo window is closed (it was open until {until}): the server will refuse an undo.
admin.log.batch.undoUnknown: The server did not name the undo deadline — we treat the window as closed until it says otherwise.
admin.log.batch.rollbackHint: We first show what will change and ask for the person's id — as in “Roles”.
admin.log.batch.rollbackClosed: This batch cannot be rolled back from here: the undo window is closed or its deadline is unknown.
admin.log.batch.rollbackNoBody: This batch cannot be rolled back from here: the server sent no rollback body.
admin.machine.title: Machine
admin.machine.noOwner: No editing: the agent has no owner, and the server links a machine only together with one.
admin.machine.noClient: No editing: the agent has no account (client_id), and the server will not accept the request without it.
admin.machine.hint: A miniLORE machine (client_id minilore-link-*) is one per name; lore-mcp-* agents on one machine share the name legitimately.
admin.roles.sources.hint: Keycloak — the person's realm roles; Forgejo is not asked yet: there is no link between the LORE user and a Forgejo user. Read-only.
admin.mcp.title: MCP
admin.mcp.lead: MCP connections and failures by agent profile — what LORE sees from calls. A profile silent for long is marked “not seen”, not “healthy”.
admin.mcp.profilesNote: These are profiles (full, pm, …), not sessions: LORE cannot tell sessions of one Keycloak client apart.
admin.mcp.emptyHint: This is not “all fine”: LORE simply has not seen a single MCP call.
admin.mcp.failError: Could not read failures ({reason}) — connections are shown, nothing is claimed about failures.
admin.mcp.truncated: Not all profiles shown: the server truncated the result.
admin.mcp.health.stale: not seen for over a day
kitPage.fields.lead: Editor by model field kind: empty ≠ zero ≠ “not set”, booleans have three states, date without zone, date-time with zone, unknown kind is read only.
kitPage.flow.lead: Wizard steps: order, a named reason when you cannot go on, going back without losing input, the step in the URL, and a final “left to do by hand” list.
kitPage.flow.s3lead: A real screen would preview the changes here.
kitPage.flow.manual1: Hand over the password in person
kitPage.flow.doneSaid: Wizard finished — the app would now perform the action.
kitPage.flow.diffUnver: This row could not be verified
kitPage.flow.diffApplied: The app received {n} row(s) — it then applies them as one batch with an undo window.
kitPage.flow.batchHead: The batch: undo window and partial failure
kitPage.flow.matrixHead: The matrix: a value in the cell and the check state
kitPage.flow.matrixLead: The matrix applies nothing: proposals go to the diff, and the diff to the batch with an undo window.
kitPage.flow.matrixProposed: Changes proposed: {n} — the diff shows them next.
kitPage.flow.chainHead: Why this verdict: the outcome and its chain of reasons
kitPage.flow.chainLead: The outcome in one line, and under it the steps in the order they decided. A step has five outcomes, not two: confirmed · ruled out · could not verify · not allowed to look · not asked. The decisive step is marked, and a chain cut short says so.
kitPage.flow.chainUnaskedWhy: the source is switched off in the settings
kitPage.flow.chainStopWhy: the rest was not computed — the outcome was already settled
kitPage.flow.relHead: Content release: version diff and activation
kitPage.flow.relLead: The release class (hotfix or release) is computed by the server — the showcase shows what was sent. Activation and rollback go through a confirmation.

admin.access.title: Effective access
admin.access.realmHint: The realm role is known to Keycloak, not the graph — take it from the KC card (viewer, editor, admin…). Empty — no realm role.
admin.access.pickHint: Pick a project — the server explains whether this person sees it and why.
admin.access.scopeOff: Project scope is off on the server — every signed-in user sees the project now.
admin.access.nobody: Nobody has a role in the project — only bypassing realm roles see it.
admin.access.bypass: Realm roles that bypass the scope:

admin.access.noAgentsSee: No agents — no projects are inherited.

admin.roles.title: Roles
admin.roles.lead: A person's roles across all their projects: groups by role, search, multi-select and a matrix. Every change goes through a diff, typing the login and a batch with undo.
admin.roles.forbidden: No permission to view people's roles
admin.roles.forbiddenHint: Only a LORE administrator (admin role) can see and change people's roles.
admin.roles.empty: No people in the graph yet
admin.roles.emptyHint: A person appears here once they are granted their first project role.
admin.roles.pick: Pick a person to open their roles card.
admin.roles.notFound: Person {id} is not in the role matrix — the link is stale or they have no roles any more.
admin.roles.rowUnverified: the server did not confirm the roles were read in full
admin.roles.none: The person has no project roles (checked in the graph).
admin.roles.noMatch: No project matches the search — roles exist, just not under this word.
admin.roles.panelHint: Nothing is applied right away: first a diff for all selected projects and one confirmation by login.
admin.roles.matrixHint: Clicking a cell or “set the whole row” is a proposal: the diff with confirmation applies it.
admin.roles.danger.title: What changes for {name}
admin.kc.logged: The action is recorded in the action log.
admin.kc.realm.title: Keycloak realm role
admin.kc.realm.unknown: Role “{role}” is not grantable — pick another
admin.kc.realm.hint: The bridge does not grant super-admin — only manually in Keycloak. Grant and removal go through a diff and typing the login; undo is possible for 15 minutes.
admin.kc.rotate.title: Rotate the secret of {client}
admin.kc.rotate.noUndo: A rotation cannot be undone — you can only issue a new secret. An agent with the old secret stops signing in at once.
admin.kc.rotate.noSecret: Keycloak answered without the secret value — the old one is most likely already invalid. Issue a new one.
admin.kc.rotate.doneNoUndo: Secret rotated. It cannot be undone — you can only issue a new one.
admin.kc.rotate.noClient: The agent has no Keycloak client (client_id) — nothing to rotate
admin.roles.danger.loading: The server is computing the diff…
admin.roles.danger.logged: The batch is recorded in the action journal.
kitPage.chips.title: Chip values
kitPage.chips.lead: A field value may arrive as an object: an id for the link, a label for the human, and a mark of inheritance. The row shows the first three, the rest sit under “N more”. An inherited chip says where it came from — “the task’s project” and “its sprint’s project” are different claims. No label means the id is shown, not emptiness.
admin.roles.all.hint: Row — project, column — person. A cell click or "set whole row/column" is a proposal: a diff with login confirmation applies it, one batch per person.
admin.roles.all.sources: Accounts outside the graph, per person
admin.roles.queue: {n} more people queued: their batches open one by one after this one.
admin.roles.role.pick: Pick a role to open its card: what it grants and who holds it.
admin.roles.role.grantsWrite: Role "{role}" in a project: sees the project and writes to it. The owner's agents write there with profiles per the D4 matrix.
admin.roles.role.grantsRead: Role "{role}" in a project: sees the project, read-only.
admin.roles.role.bypass: Realm roles admin and superadmin see every project bypassing project roles — Keycloak shows them, not this card.
admin.roles.role.nobody: Nobody holds role "{role}" now (checked against the graph).
admin.roles.role.nobodyUnverified: No holders of "{role}" found, but the server did not confirm the roles were read completely.
admin.roles.why: Why they see / do not see
admin.agentWhy.title: Why it sees
admin.agentWhy.inherits: Sees every project of its owner {owner} — inherits from them; writes where the owner's role delegates profile "{scope}" (D4).
admin.agentWhy.noowner: Sees no project: the agent has no owner — nothing to inherit from.
admin.agentWhy.noclient: The server cannot recognise it: no client_id, so the chain "account → agent → owner" has no entry.
admin.orphans.title: Orphaned agent detector findings
admin.orphans.graph: Agents without an owner in the graph ({n}) — no projects are inherited:
admin.orphans.graphNone: No agents without an owner in the graph.
admin.orphans.kc: Keycloak clients without an agent in the graph
admin.orphans.kcHint: The service account exists, but no KnowActor has this client_id: the server cannot derive any project role for it. Create the agent or disable the client.
admin.orphans.kcNone: Keycloak answered: no clients without an agent.
admin.orphans.kcForbidden: Detector not shown: no rights (admin role required).
admin.orphans.kcUnconfigured: Detector did not run: the LORE–Keycloak link is not configured on the server.
admin.bind.title: Link a client to a person
admin.bind.noScope: carries no agent scope, linking not allowed
admin.bind.summary: Profile: {profile} · machine: {machine}. The agent inherits projects from its owner.
admin.bind.noMachine: not in the name — link it in the agent card
admin.bind.done: {client} linked — the agent will appear in the list above.
admin.who.nothingHint: We match person name and login, project slug, agent name and client.
admin.machine.taken: Machine “{id}” is already used by: {agents}. If it is the same machine, that is fine; otherwise pick another name.
admin.machine.unbindAsk: Unbind machine “{id}”? The agent stays without a machine until bound again.
admin.home.title: Home
admin.home.lead: Only what is broken or unfinished. Each card leads to the screen that fixes it.
admin.home.noMachineHint: no way to tell which laptop they come from
lists.date.noTime: this section's slice does not return record change times
admin.wiz.title: Wizards
admin.wiz.lead: A scenario from intent to a “works” check — with an honest list of what is left to do by hand elsewhere.
admin.wiz.person.title: Add a person
admin.wiz.person.lead: Keycloak account → projects “like someone” → batch diff → check
admin.wiz.agent.title: Give a person an agent
admin.wiz.agent.lead: Whose → profile in words → secret once → first call
admin.wiz.machine.title: New laptop
admin.wiz.machine.lead: Machine name → agent inherits your rights → command → check → the rest
admin.wiz.person.createHint: The account is created without a password: LORE stores no passwords. The person sets it via a reset link — see “left to do by hand”.
admin.wiz.person.likeHint: Uncheck a project to skip it. Change the role in the list next to it. Unverified roles are not copied.
admin.wiz.person.diffLead: The “what changes” diff appears here — the server computes it when you reach this step.
admin.wiz.person.checkLead: Check in “People and their projects” that the person sees their projects.
admin.wiz.person.b.account: Find or create the Keycloak account first
admin.wiz.person.b.projects: Pick someone similar and keep at least one project
admin.wiz.person.b.diff: Apply the batch — or go back and uncheck what is not needed
admin.wiz.agent.ownerHint: The agent sees its owner's projects — no need to grant projects separately.
admin.wiz.agent.noProfiles: Keycloak has no profile template (client lore-mcp-<profile>) — nothing to issue an agent from.
admin.wiz.agent.inherits: Projects are inherited from the owner; no role questions.
admin.wiz.agent.noSecret: The server returned no secret. The account exists but cannot sign in without one — rotate the secret on the Agents screen.
admin.wiz.agent.linkError: The Keycloak account is created, but the agent is not linked in LORE: {reason}. Keep the secret above — link the owner on the Agents screen.
admin.wiz.agent.secretEnv: The secret in the command and the file is the LORE_MCP_CLIENT_SECRET variable: keep it in Infisical or the machine environment, never in the file.
admin.wiz.agent.checkLead: The wizard does not stop at “issued”: the check looks for a session or the first write of the agent from this machine.
admin.wiz.agent.waiting: No session or write from this machine yet. The server does not tell reads apart per account — silence means “not seen yet”, not “broken”.
admin.wiz.agent.b.machineChars: Machine name: Latin letters, digits, dot, _ and -; starts with a letter or digit
admin.wiz.agent.b.machineTaken: The name is taken by another owner's machine: {owner}
admin.wiz.machine.b.me: We do not know who you are: sign in again
admin.wiz.profile.full: full: everything your project role allows
admin.wiz.profile.developer: reads everything, writes tasks, statuses, PR links
admin.wiz.profile.unknown: no profile description — see the Keycloak template for rights
admin.wiz.manual.title: Left to do by hand
admin.wiz.manual.password: Hand over the password in person
admin.wiz.manual.passwordHint: the admin panel neither sees nor sends it: reset link or Keycloak console
admin.wiz.manual.forgejoHint: LORE does not grant Forgejo access
admin.wiz.manual.secretStore: Hand the secret to the agent's owner
admin.wiz.manual.secretStoreHint: via Infisical; not in chat or e-mail
admin.wiz.manual.mcpBuild: Clone UnlimitedLORE and build mcp-server on the machine
admin.wiz.manual.mcpBuildHint: cd mcp-server && npm ci && npm run build — put the dist/index.js path into the command
admin.wiz.manual.minilore: minilore-link — the channel to the phone
admin.wiz.manual.infisicalHint: could not check — LORE has no access to Infisical
admin.roles.danger.need: Until the login is typed exactly, nothing can be applied.
peek.err.noType: record type is not set and cannot be recognised from the ID — cannot open
admin.wiz.finished: Wizard «{title}» is finished. Pick a wizard to start again.
admin.wiz.project.title: Project like another
admin.wiz.project.lead: Register a project, check its repository in Forgejo and give people roles like in a similar project
admin.wiz.project.slugHint: usually owner/repo name; never changes later — sprints, releases and roles hang on it
admin.wiz.project.exists: Project {slug} is already registered — taking it as is; registering again would overwrite its fields
admin.wiz.project.name: Name
admin.wiz.project.registerError: Not registered: {reason}. Registering a project takes superadmin or the full agent (project_new)
admin.wiz.project.repoLead: Does the Forgejo bridge see the repository of {slug} and branch {branch}
admin.wiz.project.repoMissing: Not found: no repository, no branch, or the bridge token has no access — the server does not tell these apart ({reason})
admin.wiz.project.repoUnresolvable: The bridge cannot tell where the repository is: the project has no primary host ({reason})
admin.wiz.project.repoUnchecked: Could not check: {reason}. This does not mean there is no repository — open Forgejo via the link
admin.wiz.project.like: People and roles as in project
admin.wiz.project.nobody: Nobody has a role in {project} — nothing to copy
admin.wiz.project.roleOf: Role of {name} in the new project
admin.wiz.project.likeHint: Checked — grant a role in {slug}; the role can be changed. Unverified roles are not copied
admin.wiz.project.applyLead: One batch per person in turn: diff, login to confirm, apply; undo while the window is open
admin.wiz.project.verdict.some: Granted {n} of {total}; the rest were skipped or undone
admin.wiz.project.verdict.partial: Partially granted: fully {n} of {total}; failed for: {who}
admin.wiz.project.b.slugChars: slug takes only Latin letters, digits and _ . / -
admin.wiz.project.b.projectsUnknown: could not read the project list — cannot tell whether an existing one would be overwritten
admin.wiz.project.b.people: pick a similar project and at least one person
admin.wiz.project.b.apply: {n} people still undecided: apply the batch or close it
admin.wiz.project.manual.access: Forgejo: people's access to the repository
admin.wiz.project.manual.accessHint: LORE does not grant Forgejo access: add everyone listed as collaborators or to a team
admin.wiz.project.manual.createHint: if it does not exist yet; then re-check the Repository step
admin.dicts.title: Dictionaries
admin.dicts.lead: LORE dictionaries are the language of the whole system: labels, colours and icons of statuses, areas, profiles. An edit shows on every screen at once; a value's code is a data key and is not editable.
admin.dicts.truncated: The dictionary answer was cut by the limit — not all values are shown.
admin.dicts.usageError: Could not count area usage: components were not read ({reason}). This is not "0 uses".
admin.dicts.newTypeBad: code — lowercase latin, digits and "_", starting with a letter
admin.dicts.newTypeHint: the type appears together with its first value
admin.dicts.canonWarn: Canon dictionary (ADR-LORE-010): values are built into the statuses of the whole corpus. Label, colour and icon can be edited — after typing the value code; codes are never edited.
admin.dicts.emptyB: The slice answered with no rows.
admin.dicts.col.label: label
admin.dicts.usageNA: The server counts usage only for area; not for this dictionary.
admin.dicts.reactivateNote: The value is off now — "Apply" turns it back on.
admin.dicts.preview: This is how it will look
admin.dicts.iconBad: No icon with this name — it will be blank.
admin.dicts.usageWarn: {n} components carry this code. Changing colour or icon changes their look across LORE.
admin.dicts.usageWarnUnknown: Could not count how many records carry this code. The edit may affect all of them.
admin.dicts.confirmCanon: Canon dictionary: the edit affects the whole corpus. Type the code "{code}" to apply
admin.dicts.confirmDeact: Deactivating a value. Type the code "{code}" to apply
admin.tags.note: Read-only: merging and renaming tags is done with MCP tools; there is no UI editor.
admin.tags.truncated: The tags answer was cut by the limit — not all are shown.
admin.tags.empty: No tags (the slice answered with an empty list)
admin.pf.title: Enabling authentication
admin.pf.admins: At least one person has the admin role
admin.pf.adminsUnknown: admin count unknown: the Keycloak bridge is not configured or did not answer
admin.pf.adminsN: Now: {n}. Add yourself and grant the admin role.
admin.pf.kcOff: Bridge not configured: KC_ADMIN_CLIENT_SECRET is not set.
admin.pf.scope: Agent rights are checked on the backend
admin.pf.scopeOn: AgentScopeFilter is on: the agent_scope claim is checked on every request.
admin.pf.scopeOff: AgentScopeFilter is not working: without OIDC there is nothing to check.
admin.pf.authOff: Auth: off — dev mode, role from config.
admin.pf.enableNote: The flip itself is env LORE_AUTH_ENABLED=true and a restart per RUNBOOK-AUTH-OMILORE, all flags together (AL-12 — owner in person). There is no UI button: the server has no runtime switch.
admin.pf.activeProject: LORE_ACTIVE_PROJECT is the session default project of the MCP process (env, ADR-LORE-017): set in .mcp.json or the OpenCode config, not readable from the UI.
admin.denials.title: Recent access denials
admin.denials.src: Source: process memory since the last restart (ring buffer of 401/403/409, AL-45) — not an audit. The long-term action log is above.
admin.denials.forbidden: Only the admin role sees denials.
admin.denials.empty: No denials since the last restart
admin.set.title: Application settings
admin.set.lead: app_setting dictionary keys that LORE reads: chart layer, Völva address, Forgejo Actions polling, images in MD. A key without a record is "not set" and the default applies.
admin.set.bad.url: An http:// or https:// address is required
admin.set.bad.choice: Only echarts or volva are allowed
admin.set.def.volvaUrl: — (no Völva button on the decision card)
admin.set.descr.volvaUrl: Völva address for links from LORE: "Documents in Völva" and "Document for the decision" on the decision card. They open in the user's session, with the user's Völva rights.
admin.set.hint.volvaUrl: http(s) only. Takes effect after a page reload.
admin.set.descr.chartLayer: What draws LORE charts: echarts — LORE itself from its own data; volva — embedded Völva charts (needs a card in Völva and the lore.volva.embed.charts whitelist on the backend).
admin.set.hint.chartLayer: One setting for the whole of LORE, takes effect after a page reload. If the Völva layer has no such chart, "not configured" is shown instead of an empty frame.
admin.set.descr.qgProjects: Which repositories the Forgejo Actions run channel polls for quality gates. Empty — Actions runs are not written into gates.
admin.set.hint.qgProjects: slug like owner/repo. The edit is picked up on the next polling round, without a restart.
admin.set.descr.mdImages: Whether images may be inserted into MD fields (descriptions, notes, doc bodies). false — uploads answer MD_IMAGES_DISABLED.
admin.set.hint.mdImages: Takes effect at once, no restart: the value is read on every upload.
admin.set.descr.mdImageMax: Maximum size of one image in an MD field. Larger — the upload is rejected with the file size in the answer.
admin.set.unknownB: These keys are in the database (dict_type=app_setting) but the application does not read them — most likely left over from a manual edit. Removal is a soft-delete (is_active=false).
admin.set.removeDetail: is_active=false — the record stays in history
admin.set.volva.note: Requests a signed address of the pilot velocity chart — the same path as the Völva layer.
admin.set.volva.ok: Done: the address was issued, leads to {origin}, valid until {expires}.
admin.set.volva.notConfigured: Not configured: the backend has no LORE_VOLVA_EMBED_SECRET secret or lore.volva.embed.site-url address. ({d})
admin.set.volva.unknownChart: The velocity chart is not in the lore.volva.embed.charts whitelist. ({d})
admin.quick.title: Quick commands
admin.quick.note: A personal cheat sheet — everyday commands so the order need not be recalled. The command is shown in full; "Copy" puts it on the clipboard.
admin.quick.attach: Attach the console to a dialogue by sessionId (shown in the app) via the minilore-link channel — NOT -c, it picks the wrong dialogue. PowerShell.
admin.quick.unavailable: Not copied: the clipboard is unavailable (the page is not on https/localhost). Select the command manually.
admin.quick.failed: Not copied: the browser denied clipboard access. Select the command manually.
admin.projects.title: Projects
admin.projects.lead: Who is in each project, with which role, and whose agents work there. An agent sees all of its owner’s projects, so a project runs the agents of all its members. Expand a project to see who sees it and why.
admin.mcp.fails.title: Agent write refusals (code ≥ 400)
admin.mcp.fails.error: Could not read the refusal list: {reason}
admin.mcp.fails.emptyHint: no agent writes answered with code ≥ 400 were observed
admin.mcp.fails.shown: Showing {n} of {m} — the count on the Home screen
admin.mcp.fails.shownNoTotal: Showing {n}; the total could not be read
admin.roles.noProjectsEmptyHint: every checked account has at least one role
admin.off.title: Offboard {name}
admin.off.lead: First see everything this person holds; then remove it block by block — each with a diff and the login typed to confirm.
admin.off.kc.willDisable: will be disabled, open sessions closed
admin.off.lastOwner: This is the last owner of project {project}. Without an owner nobody can manage the project — assign another owner before removing this one.
admin.off.agents.noClient: the agent has no Keycloak account (client_id) — nothing to disable
admin.off.agents.absent: no Keycloak client with this clientId
admin.off.agents.reversible: A disabled agent account stops getting tokens at once. It can be reverted: “Undo” after applying enables it again with the same secret.
admin.off.realm.none: the account has no LORE realm roles
admin.off.realm.d11: super-admin is not removed through the bridge (D11) — only by hand in the Keycloak console.
admin.off.lastAdmin: This is the last enabled account with the admin/super-admin role — removing it leaves LORE without an administrator. Make someone else admin first (AL-35).
admin.off.self: This is you. You cannot offboard yourself here: the last project role and the last admin role are guarded by the server (AL-100, AL-35) — ask another administrator.
admin.off.manual.title: Left to do by hand
admin.off.machines.none: No machines: owns none and is granted on none (checked)
admin.off.machines.owned: Owns machines: {list}. Revoking access does not remove ownership — it is listed under «left to do by hand».
admin.off.machines.noGrants: No access to other people's machines (checked)
admin.off.manual.machine: Hand over or remove machine {machine} — this person owns it
admin.off.manual.machineHint: the machine owner is changed in «Agents»: LORE has no request that removes ownership
kitPage.cal.head: Calendar
kitPage.cal.lead: Month grid: up to three records per day, then “N more”; records without a date are counted. The app decides which field is the date.
kitPage.mini.head: Mini list
kitPage.mini.lead: One component for todo and quiz: checkmarks and “N of M done”; pick an option, after answering — the correct one and a hint for the wrong one. Items and the answer are app data.
kitPage.mini.q1: All rows on the left, even without a match
kitPage.lib.head: Library
kitPage.lib.lead: An owner’s documents by kind: groups on the left, reading in place on the right, a bottom sheet on a phone. The first five per group, then “N more”; the app names the owner, the groups and what “stale” means.
kitPage.lib.body1: List columns drifted: width and order were set per screen. **Decision:** the model describes how a column shows — priority, width step and overflow.
create.newHint: New record — in the same panel as “Read in full”
create.note: Only what a record cannot be created without. After saving, the full record opens: links, properties and the rest are edited there.
create.field.title: Title
create.err.exists: A record with code “{{id}}” already exists — not overwriting. Open it from the list or pick another code.
create.err.unchecked: Could not check whether the code is free ({{reason}}) — not sent, so as not to overwrite someone else’s record.
create.err.forbidden: No right to create a record ({{reason}})
create.err.refused: The server did not accept the record ({{reason}})
create.sprints.failed: The sprint list did not load ({{reason}}) — nothing to pick, the task cannot be created now.
create.sprints.empty: No open sprints — nowhere to put the task.
create.sprints.cut: The sprint list was cut by the server — not all are shown.
admin.macl.title: Machine access
admin.macl.lead: Who can see a miniLORE machine's dialogues and act in them. Access is granted and revoked by the machine owner or an admin.
admin.macl.emptyHint: A machine appears once an agent with a minilore-link-* client is set up in Agents.
admin.macl.truncated: Not all machines arrived: the result is truncated.
admin.macl.partial: People's projects failed to load ({reason}): machine projects come from grants only; granting and the matrix have no teams.
admin.macl.notFound: Machine “{id}” is not in the result
admin.macl.notFoundHint: It may have been removed or renamed; the list above is what exists now.
admin.macl.noOwner: no owner — only an admin can grant access
admin.macl.grants.title: Grants · {n} people + owner
admin.macl.grants.note: A person granted several projects appears in each of their groups, so the groups add up to more than the total.
admin.macl.grants.empty: No grants (checked): only the owner sees this machine
admin.macl.grants.emptyHint: You can grant people access below.
admin.macl.form.title: Grant access
admin.macl.right.checking: Checking whether you may grant access…
admin.macl.right.unknown: Could not check whether you may grant access: {reason}. Read only for now.
admin.macl.right.noSlice: access to this machine is granted only by its owner or an admin
admin.macl.right.unknownSlice: the server could not compute rights for this machine
admin.macl.change.title: What will change
admin.macl.change.loading: The server is computing the plan…
admin.macl.change.undoNote: The change was applied as one server batch; undo restores the previous grants for the whole batch while its window is open.
admin.macl.matrix.noAccess: with no access to any project machine: {n}
admin.macl.matrix.note: Editing a cell is a proposal: the server shows the plan and checks the right itself (machine owner or admin).
admin.macl.person.title: Machines · owns {owned} · granted {granted}
admin.macl.person.none: No machines: owns none and has no grants (checked)

admin.why.title: Why it can't see — agent or tool
admin.why.lead: The chain the server decides by: account → agent → owner → owner's role in the project → does that role delegate the agent's profile.
admin.why.toolHint: adr_new, task_set or a family (adr, task)
admin.why.pick: Pick an agent and a project — we'll show why it does or doesn't see the project.
admin.why.pickTool: Pick an agent, a project and a tool — or a 403 refusal row below.
admin.why.step.tool: Tool: which family it writes and which profiles may write it
admin.why.step.role: Owner's role in the project — the agent reads
admin.why.step.delegate: Owner's role delegates the agent profile (D4) — the agent writes
admin.why.toolNoServer: the server did not answer whether the agent profile writes to “{tool}” — could not check
admin.why.noClient: the agent has no client_id — it can't enter the server's chain
admin.why.ownerNoRole: the owner has no role in project {project}
admin.why.ownerRoleUnknown: project is visible, the server didn't name the role
admin.why.noProfile: agent profile (agent_role) is not set — nothing to check against the matrix
admin.why.notDelegates: "{role}" does not delegate profile {profile}; it delegates: {profiles}
admin.why.stopNoEntry: without an account the rest was not checked
admin.why.stopNoAnswer: the server didn't answer — nothing to check the rest with
admin.why.stopNoOwner: without an owner projects are not inherited — the rest was not checked
admin.why.stopNoRole: the project is not visible — delegation was not checked
admin.why.verdict.toolUnknown: {agent} has access to project {project}, but the server didn't explain the tool — not verified
admin.why.fixRole: Fix: owner's role in the project
admin.why.roleNeedSee: Owner {owner} has no role in project {project} — the agent can't see it. Grant the owner a role.
admin.why.roleNeedDelegate: Owner {owner}'s role in project {project} is "{role}", which doesn't delegate the agent's profile. Change the role.
admin.why.roleNoServerHint: The server doesn't list which roles delegate this profile — check the diff and the chain after applying.
admin.why.ownerConfirm: Type the agent name "{agent}" to bind
admin.why.ownerDone: {owner} owns agent {agent}. The chain was recomputed.
admin.why.ownerNotLinked: The server did not bind the owner: {hint}
admin.why.ownerNoUndo: No undo: the server can set an owner but not remove one (POST /lore/actor/owner). If wrong — bind another.
admin.why.recent403Hint: profile → family · record · time (UTC). A row fills the family into the tool field.
admin.why.no403: No 403 refusals in the last day
admin.why.home403Hint: agent writes refused by the server; profiles: {n}
admin.why.stopTool: the tool is closed to the profile — project and owner were not checked
admin.why.verdict.toolDenied: {agent} cannot write with this tool: the agent profile closes it, project {project} is not the cause
admin.why.profileNeed: Profile {current} does not write to “{tool}”. Open to profiles: {profiles}.
admin.why.profileHint: The agent profile is a Keycloak client role; it changes by issuing an account of the needed profile. The “Agent for a person” wizard shows the plan and asks for confirmation.
admin.why.humanOnly: “{tool}” is edited by a human only — no agent profile writes here. Do it yourself in the admin.
admin.why.row.allowed: profile {profile} writes to “{what}” — the refusal is not from the profile matrix but from the project (the owner role does not delegate the profile)
admin.why.row.unlisted: “{what}” is outside the profile matrix — the refusal did not come from the profile filter
admin.why.row.no_profile: the caller has no agent profile
